title: The Invitation
sceneText:
Early in the morning a messenger rides over from Millridge with a formally worded letter.

The wax carries the Duke’s arms: the hunting season is a duchy occasion, and the invitation goes out in the duchy’s form. But the writing inside is in Baron Henk’s own hand, broad and open, like an invitation between neighbours. It says that Maplegate’s family steward takes part in the season every year, and he hopes the custom will hold.

“The camp is pitched at the hunting ground on the east side of the ducal woods. Opening this afternoon, five days, until sundown on the twenty-second of October.”

Gregor puts his head out of the stable.

{@gregor}“That letter comes every year.” He commits to nothing either way. “Mr Hartmann attended seven years running. The eighth, he found a reason not to.”

There is a line appended at the foot of the letter, in smaller and looser writing than the body:

“Her Grace the Duke will be present at the opening this year.”

{@gregor}“Her Grace comes every year.” He glances at the line. “She has never once come over to our side.”

effects.logEntry: You changed into riding dress and went to the ducal hunting ground after noon.

choices.text: Send back a properly worded apology

effects.logEntry: You wrote an apology and sent it back with the messenger.

choices.resultText:
You write a reply, taking a while over the wording: the harvest is at its height, the estate is short of hands, with regrets, and next year without fail.

You give the letter to the messenger to take back. He is a little surprised as he takes it, but asks nothing.

Gregor is standing in the stable doorway.

{@gregor}“Answered it?”

You say you did.

{@gregor}“Mm.”

He turns and goes in. You cannot tell whether he approves.

Three days later at the market somebody says that eleven men came to the north district’s hunting season this year. Other years it is twelve.

choices.text: Make no answer, and get on with the estate

effects.logEntry: You did not answer the letter from Millridge.

choices.resultText:
You put the letter on the desk and go and see to other things.

The messenger waited in the courtyard for nearly an hour. Martha brought him water. In the end he left on his own.

At dusk Martha said, in the kitchen, that you had still not answered the letter from Millridge.

You said there was no need.

She said “oh”, and asked no more.
